newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo palladium futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo palladium futures end mostly lower.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo palladium futures ended mostly lower on Thursday, with the December 1997 contract down by the daily limit of 22 yen, as profit-taking by local investors capped the topside, traders said.
The benchmark June 1998 contract was down 21 yen at 543 yen per gram. The exception was the spot July, which was up six yen at 736 yen at the closing.

Profit-taking by local investors, following Wednesday's price gains, pushed down palladium futures prices, traders said. Platinum futures ended mixed, with the June 1998 down two yen at 1,363 yen per gram.

Russia's metal export agency Almazjuvelierexport plans to send platinum to Japan for arrival by Monday, local traders said. It will be the first shipment of platinum from Russia to Japan in about six months.
Gold futures ended unchanged to eight yen lower, with the benchmark June 1998 down three yen at 1,185 yen per gram.
Bullion was quoted $320.75/321.25 per ounce at 0753 GMT, compared with $322.75/25 in New York on Wednesday.
Traders said that lower bullion prices turned TOCOM gold futures' sentiment bearish. "We're watching how gold prices move this evening," a brokerage house trader said.
